newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba sees high Red River flood risk-government.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba sees high Red River flood risk-government.

text.p: There is a high risk of flooding along Manitoba's Red River and its tributaries during this spring's thaw because of heavy winter snowfall and water-saturated soil, a provincial government official said.

"There's a 10 percent chance this could be the worst flood this century. It is kind of disturbing. It all depends upon the weather for the next month to six weeks," Manitoba Natural Resources flood liaison officer Larry Whitney told reporters.
Twice the average amount of snowfall accumulated in the Red River basin in Canada and three times the average amount fell in the United States this winter, Whitney said.
North Dakota issued a flood watch, he said.
Wheat, canola, oats and corn are primary crops grown in the portion of southeast Manitoba that could be affected.
The temperature level, amount of precipitation and timing of river ice breakup in the next six weeks will determine the severity of spring flooding on the Red and tributary rivers.
Tributaries like the Morris, Lasalle, Roseau and Pembina rivers were included in the high flood risk, Whitney said.
The Shellmouth Dam in southeast Manitoba was being drawn down to last year's pre-flood level to store water, he added.
"We'll be using the Portage Diversion, I can virtually guarantee that and the (Winnipeg) Floodway," Whitney said.
The Assiniboine and Souris rivers further west in Manitoba also had a risk of flooding but were comparable to last year's level, he said.
